name: Zeal-Colossus
geological_features: Bands of metallic hydrogen storms circling the equator
A permanent anticyclone three times the diameter of most terrestrial worlds
Liquid helium rain in the upper atmosphere
specific_features: Atmospheric fauna of enormous scale, visible from orbital distance
description: Zeal-Colossus is a gas giant of staggering proportion, its banded atmosphere a roiling canvas of metallic hydrogen storms and liquid helium precipitation that spans a diameter of one hundred and thirty-eight thousand kilometers. The permanent anticyclone that dominates its southern hemisphere is itself larger than most habitable worlds, a storm system of such scale that it has persisted for millions of years.

The dense atmosphere screams with wind speeds that exceed the speed of sound in the upper layers, creating a world of perpetual violent motion that seems to vibrate with manic energy. There is nothing restful about Zeal-Colossus; it is a planet that does everything at maximum intensity, every system pushed to extremes.

Atmospheric fauna inhabit the middle cloud layers, gas-bag organisms of extraordinary size that filter nutrients from the chemical soup of the mid-atmosphere. The largest specimens exceed fifty kilometers in length, their translucent bodies visible from orbit as they drift through the storm bands with a serenity that belies the violence around them.

The helium-3 reserves in the upper atmosphere could fuel human civilization for millennia, but harvesting operations must contend with winds that shred conventional materials and fauna large enough to engulf collection vessels whole. The zealous energy of this world resists exploitation with the same intensity that makes its resources so desperately coveted.
